question.problem:
Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-x+1 & \text{ for }\,x\le 0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x+1 & \text{ for }\,x>0.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-x+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(-x+1) \\  & =-(0)+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, approaching from the right, we have $x>0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡0+1 \\  & =0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)=1.
$$
